title: How tap to pay works without sending your real card number
description: Contactless payments use a short-range radio link and a stand-in code instead of your real card number.

scenes.big: Tap to pay: no card number sent
scenes.say: When you tap your phone to pay, your real card number usually isn't what gets sent. Something clever is.

First, the link. Near field communication is a short-range radio at 13.56 megahertz. It typically works within a few centimeters, which makes eavesdropping harder. It can even power a battery-less tag.

steps: Phone holds a token, not your card
scenes.say: Second, the data. Your phone sends a token, a digital stand-in for your card. Each payment also creates its own one-time code. So an intercepted token is useless for another purchase.
Typical range is about four centimeters, so a snoop would need to be nearly touching your phone.

Even if someone grabbed it, they couldn't replay it elsewhere. The short range, the token, and the one-time code all work together. So your phone stays useful, and your real number stays hidden. Follow for more tech, explained simply.
